registered: 2026-10-16, after the teaching material (L committed 76c6b2f before the research; G in the commit that adds this file) and BEFORE any Stage 4 request was collected or read. Code, teaching and scorer are frozen at the commit that adds this file.
question: On untouched real requests about the two pilot categories, does research-guided teaching (G) beat vocabulary-based teaching (L) and the current system (BASE), especially on formulations that do not contain the category names, and does it add false needs or harmful decisions?

arms.BASE: current system: CATEGORY_REGISTRY250 + ADOPTED_LESSONS250, no pilot teaching (scripts/phase252-teaching-arms.mjs --arm BASE)
arms.L: BASE + LEXICAL_L252 (names and need phrases; written before the research)
arms.G: BASE + RESEARCH_GUIDED_G252 (same names, phrase count not above L per category: microwave_ovens 31, headphones 34; plus requirements, measures, declared-attribute relations, questions, contrasting phrases)

stores: each arm on its own copy of the current verified snapshot (pee-knowledge 4c78d47: Phase251 category assignment and the Phase252 identity split), so declarations are identical across arms
name_control: L and G share exactly the same category names. Results are reported separately for requests containing one of those names and for requests without them (formulations not present as aliases)

collection.source: Stack Exchange API only (site pages never fetched); evaluation use; CC BY-SA attribution per case
collection.excluded_ids: every id excluded for set 5 plus every set 5 and 5b pool id
collection.order: within a stratum, sha256('252t:<question_id>') ascending; a question already in an earlier stratum is skipped
collection.text: as set 5 (title + body, plain text, at most 1,500 characters)
collection.screening_and_roles: as set 5: IN_SCOPE (choosing a product of the pilot category), CLARIFY, CONFUSING_CONTROL (names the product, purchase is an accessory, part or adjacent product such as an amplifier, DAC, ear pads or a microwave-safe container), OUT_OF_SCOPE_CONTROL; exclusions recorded with reasons
collection.quotas: per pilot category at most 20 IN_SCOPE or CLARIFY, 8 CONFUSING_CONTROL, 5 OUT_OF_SCOPE_CONTROL
collection.insufficiency: target at least 12 in-scope cases per pilot category; a shortfall is reported, no re-query

gold.need_catalogue: the union of the L and G need ids (both arms' ids are subsets): microwave_ovens: batch_capacity, small_kitchen, fast_heating, even_heating, ease_of_use, cleaning_effort, grill_browning, defrosting, radiation_safety; headphones: noise_cancelling, comfort, sound_quality, battery_life, wireless, durability, microphone_calls, portability, sport_fit, hearing_safety. Definitions as the statements in src/phase252_category_teaching.ts; other needs are unlisted.
gold.explicit_vs_implicit: explicitNeeds: stated in words that name the need itself ("noise cancelling", "heats evenly"); implicitNeeds: implied by a situation or problem ("I commute on a loud train", "the middle stays frozen")
gold.requirements: derived automatically from gold needs by the scorer rubric REQUIREMENT_OF (not labelled by hand)
gold.author: Claude, from the excerpt text only, before any arm runs; T2: not author-independent, not adjudicated

scoring.script: scripts/phase252-teaching-score.mjs as committed with this protocol
dimensions: incorrect inferred needs (count, precision, on controls)
technical requirements (rubric REQUIREMENT_OF: recall, false requirements)
applicability (rubric APPLICABILITY_NEEDS: a caution on the need)
declared specifications (products with a comparable declaration for each derived requirement)
missing evidence (rubric MISSING_EVIDENCE_NEEDS: flagged in the research plan)
cost (runtime, phrase budget, items and relations added)
scoring.construction_caveat: requirements, applicability and missing-evidence rubrics come from the Phase252 research; BASE and L cannot meet them by construction (they measure a capability G adds, not generalisation). Generalisation is judged on category, needs and decisions, in particular on requests without the category names.
scoring.uncertainty: counts with denominators; paired better/worse/same; no significance claims

after_first_run: first-run results committed unchanged; the Stage 4 set is then spent
